constitutive_assumptions: Silicone rubber material is isotropic and incompressible (I3 = 1)
Silicone rubber mechanical behavior is linear within a small strain range
Axial tensile deformation of the grasping unit is much larger than radial expansion, so radial deformation is assumed to be zero (lambda2 = 1 / lambda1)
Higher-order small terms in the stress tensor derivation are neglected
Stress across each grasping unit is assumed to be uniform
The length of the variable stiffness layer (VSL) is assumed to remain constant during bending

The moment generated by the internal structure of the variable stiffness layer (VSL) is negligible compared to the total unit moment because its bending direction is fully flexible without boundary constraints
control_variables: Prototype geometric parameters: la = 15 mm, lb = 3 mm, lc = 1.5 mm, ld = 10.6 mm, r1 = 8.5 mm
Silicone rubber material constants: C10 = 0.11, C01 = 0.02
Ambient atmospheric pressure during normal-pressure states
Gripper configuration (two identical VSSGU fingers mounted side-by-side)
Cantilever mounting boundary conditions during bending and stiffness tests
dependent_variables: Bending angle of the grasping unit (theta)
Bending deformation / deflection under lateral and directional loads

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Coupling a folded plate mechanism (FPM) with particle jamming inside segmented chambers provides anisotropic rigidity, allowing adaptive planar bending while resisting lateral and torsional loads and preventing particle accumulation.
Applying variable stiffness via vacuum particle jamming increases the maximum grasping weight of the soft gripper in each direction by more than three times compared to the unjammed state.
Under an 800 g cantilever load, the difference in bending angle between unjammed and jammed variable stiffness states exceeds 17 degrees.

The soft grasping unit integrated with the FPM maintains straightness without noticeable bending deformation under lateral loads of 200 g and 400 g, whereas units without FPM deform noticeably under 200 g load.

An analytical double-layer moment balance model based on Mooney-Rivlin hyperelasticity relates the positive actuation pressure and negative vacuum pressure to the bending angle, matching the trends of experimental data.
The variable stiffness soft grasping unit achieves a bending angle of more than 60 degrees when actuated by positive air pressure in the bending driving layer.

experimental_setup: Comparative lateral and directional load-bearing test fixture evaluating grasping units with and without FPM under 200 g and 400 g loads before and after stiffening

Bending characterization test rig featuring a vertically clamped VSSGU, a tip-mounted gyroscope for angle measurement, and a pneumatic proportional valve regulating BDL positive pressure and VSL vacuum pressures (-0.004 MPa and -0.008 MPa)
Variable stiffness cantilever deflection test platform with a tip gyroscope measuring angle changes under suspended weights up to 800 g before and after VSL vacuum activation
Multidirectional grasping test using a two-finger gripper to adaptively grasp a fragile ceramic vase in various orientations
Payload test grasping a beaker with incremental internal weights to determine maximum grasping capacity before and after jamming
Mobile robot platform integrating the two-finger soft gripper onto a lifting and rotating mechanism mounted on a Mecanum-wheeled car
future_work: Subsequent control and precise trajectory/force execution of the variable stiffness soft gripper using the established theoretical model
independent_variables: Input air pressure in the bending driving layer (Pi)
Vacuum pressure in the variable stiffness layer (Pj, e.g., 0 MPa, -0.004 MPa, -0.008 MPa)
Applied external weight / suspended payload (0 g up to 800 g)
Presence or absence of the folded plate mechanism (FPM)
Stiffness state (unjammed at atmospheric pressure vs. jammed under negative pressure)
limitations_inferred: The stiffening effect of vacuum jamming decreases at larger pre-bending angles, which may limit variable stiffness effectiveness when grasping bulky objects that require high initial bending.
The analytical mechanics model neglects radial expansion and higher-order strain energy terms, which could lead to discrepancies under very large multi-axis deformations.
The requirement for simultaneous positive driving pressure and negative vacuum pressure necessitates external pumps, valves, and tubing, potentially restricting portability.
Specific particle properties (material composition, particle size distribution, packing density) and elastic film durability under long-term cyclic loading are not reported in the paper.
limitations_stated_by_authors: As the bending angle increases, the effect of variable stiffness decreases; when the gripper is bent tightly to fit an object, the inward bending angle change under variable stiffness diminishes.
main_results: The VSSGU achieves a wide bending range exceeding 60 degrees.
Under an 800 g cantilever load, the difference in bending angle before and after applying variable stiffness exceeds 17 degrees, with the divergence growing as load increases.
The integration of the FPM provides structural resistance against lateral and oblique bending, preventing significant deformation under 200 g and 400 g loads.
The maximum grasping weight in multidirectional grasping is increased by more than three times (over 300%) with variable stiffness activated.
Partitioning the particle chambers with the FPM eliminates particle accumulation and facilitates rapid self-recovery of particles to their initial state upon releasing negative pressure.
Experimental bending angle curves as a function of positive drive pressure and negative vacuum pressure agree with the theoretical double-layer moment balance model predictions.
modeling_methods: Mooney-Rivlin strain energy density function model (binomial third-order expansion based on phenomenological hyperelastic theory) for silicone rubber
Uniaxial tensile test to determine rubber material constants (C10 = 0.11, C01 = 0.02)
Kinematic elongation analysis of single and serial grasping units under constant VSL length assumption
Double-layer moment balance formulation equating material resistance moment (Msr) with bending driving layer moment (Mdl) and variable stiffness layer moment (Mvs)
performance_metrics: Bending angle variation under load before and after variable stiffness (degrees)
Maximum grasping weight / payload capacity (g or fold-change)
Bending deformation / deflection under lateral and directional loads (visual straightness / deformation extent)
possible_gap_implications: Combining rigid foldable skeletons (such as folded plate mechanisms) with granular jamming modules offers a viable structural paradigm to overcome low lateral stiffness and poor multidirectional payload capacity in soft pneumatic grippers without sacrificing surface compliance.
Segmenting particle domains using rigid skeleton folds can mitigate particle settling/migration issues that commonly impair repeatability and cycle life in jamming-based soft actuators.
However, this single study does not establish generalized design rules across varied particle types, nor does it address autonomous closed-loop impedance control during dynamic manipulation.
paper.research_objective: To develop a rigid-soft coupling variable stiffness module combining a folded plate mechanism (FPM) and particle jamming within a double-layer pneumatic soft gripper structure, achieving compliant grasping, rigid multidirectional load-bearing capacity, and rapid particle recovery without accumulation.
paper.research_problem: Conventional soft grippers have low stiffness and low load capacity, causing severe bending deformation under self-weight or external load when grasping horizontally or obliquely, leading to dropped objects; additionally, conventional particle jamming grippers suffer from particle accumulation and poor recovery in flowing particle states.
paper.title: A Soft Robot With Variable Stiffness Multidirectional Grasping Based on a Folded Plate Mechanism and Particle Jamming
